territorial_scope.description: Applies to any operator that makes a chatbot available to users in South Carolina, regardless of where the operator is located.

evidence.quote: provides a chatbot to users in this State

summary.short: Adds Chapter 81 to South Carolina Code Title 39 on chatbots. Covered operators (500,000+ monthly users) must offer a limited-access mode, verify ages before enabling restricted features, add safeguards for minors, and report covered incidents to the Attorney General. Effective upon Governor's approval.
summary.long: It adds Chapter 81 to Title 39 on chatbot operators. A covered entity is an operator with 500,000 or more worldwide monthly active users, aggregated across affiliates, excluding internal, clinical, research and customer-service tools. Unverified users may access chatbots only in limited-access mode. Before enabling restricted features (personalization, proactive outreach, extended sessions, relationship simulation, explicit content), covered entities must verify age, classify users, and delete age verification data within 24 hours. Minors may use restricted features only with verifiable parental consent and parental controls. Covered entities may not design features to prioritize engagement at the expense of wellbeing, must address emotional dependence, must not falsely claim to be human, and must provide crisis messages. They must make reasonable efforts to notify emergency services about imminent risks and report covered incidents to the Attorney General within fifteen days. The Attorney General may seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation, with each day a separate violation. Harmed persons and parents of harmed minors may sue for damages, fees, and punitive damages for wilful, reckless or grossly negligent violations. Waivers of these rights are void. The act takes effect upon the Governor's approval.

relations.note: Adds new Chapter 81 (Chatbot Usage), Sections 39-81-10 through 39-81-60, to Title 39.

notes: Bill text as introduced; no later version was provided. Relations are limited to Title 39 of the S.C. Code and Chapter 4, Title 30, neither of which is in the registry. Internal inconsistencies: Section 39-81-20(C) and Section 39-81-50(A)(1) address an operator, while the rest of the chapter addresses a covered entity; Section 39-81-50(A)(1) sets a 24-hour duty on the operator although its lead-in refers to a covered entity. Section 39-81-20(B)(2) is made subject to item (3), which relies on data produced under item (2). Section 4 makes the act effective on approval by the Governor, with no fixed date. The section_status relations entry is not_applicable only because the field is required by schema; relations are recorded in the relations array.

thresholds.value_text: five hundred thousand or more monthly active users worldwide
thresholds.measurement: Unique users who interact with a chatbot at least once in a thirty-day period, per the operator's ordinary business records; aggregated across all chatbots of the covered entity and its affiliates (Sec. 39-81-10(6)(b)); worldwide
thresholds.consequence: Operator becomes a covered entity subject to the chapter's duties
thresholds.conditions: Excludes chatbots not offered to the general public and chatbots used solely for customer service (Sec. 39-81-10(6)(a)(i)-(ii))

evidence.quote: an operator of a chatbot that has five hundred thousand or more monthly active users worldwide

thresholds.consequence: Covered entity shall require the consenting parent to provide contact information or establish a linked parental account
thresholds.conditions: Applies where the user is classified as a minor and parental consent is obtained under Sec. 39-81-30(C)
